rows.figure_or_rule: This skill computes Montenegro personal income tax for an individual or a sole proprietor (preduzetnik) for 2026. The law is the Personal Income Tax Law (Zakon o porezu na dohodak fizičkih lica, "PIT Law"), consolidated through amendment 160/25, which applies from 1 January 2026 (160/25 art. 21), read with amendment 70/26, which changes the gambling rate from 21 May 2026 (70/26 arts. 1 and 3). The tax is run by the Tax Administration (Poreska uprava). The currency is the euro.

Citizenship, a bank account or one immigration document does not decide residence.

rows.figure_or_rule: Checks: a monthly salary of EUR 1,200 bears PIT of 300 × 9% + 200 × 15% = EUR 57.00. Annual principal-business profit of EUR 8,400 bears no tax; EUR 12,000 bears EUR 324.00. The salary bands are monthly; the business bands are annual. Never apply one to the other.

rows.figure_or_rule: Taxable income is total income less recognised expenses, which must be documented unless the law says otherwise (art. 13). A resident's base is the taxable income of the period less a carried-forward loss; a nonresident's base has no loss deduction (art. 8). Each income class has its own base, rate and payment route, so keep a separate schedule per class.

rows.figure_or_rule: - **Who.** A principal independent activity is a registered business, a liberal profession (health workers, vets, farmers, lawyers, notaries, auditors, engineers, architects, advisers, consultants, translators, journalists and similar) or professional and intellectual services that are the taxpayer's main activity (art. 16(2) and (3)). Supplementary entrepreneurship is business carried on by an entrepreneur as a supplementary activity under the company law (art. 16(4), added by [160/25 art. 5][amend]). Supplementary entrepreneurship is taxed at a flat 15%: it does not get the 0% and 9% bands.

rows.review_basis: Unchanged claim and evidence from original full167-group review, verified byte/hash preservation
rows.figure_or_rule: - **Base.** Taxable profit is the income-statement profit adjusted under the PIT Law (art. 17). Income and expenses follow the income statement under the accounting law unless the PIT Law says otherwise (arts. 18 and 20(1)). Dividends and profit shares from other legal persons are left out of the business base (art. 19); this does not exempt an individual's private dividends, which are capital income under art. 37.

rows.review_basis: Unchanged claim and evidence from original full167-group review, verified byte/hash preservation
rows.figure_or_rule: - **Not deductible** (art. 21): costs not incurred for the business, costs that cannot be documented, interest for late payment of tax and contributions, interest paid to nonresidents above the usual commercial rate, payments to a nonresident head office, profit distributions to employees or others, fines and penalties, and contributions to political organisations. Income tax and owner drawings are not expenses either.

rows.review_basis: Unchanged claim and evidence from original full167-group review, verified byte/hash preservation
rows.figure_or_rule: - **Inventory.** Materials and goods sold use weighted average cost or FIFO (art. 22).

rows.review_basis: Unchanged claim and evidence from original full167-group review, verified byte/hash preservation
rows.figure_or_rule: - **Depreciation.** Tax depreciation replaces book depreciation on fixed assets over EUR 200 with a life over one year, at the group rates in the table (art. 23). Right-of-use assets under operating leases and intangible assets are depreciated as booked under the accounting rules (art. 23(6) and (7)). Do not use the corporate-tax EUR 300 threshold.

rows.review_basis: Unchanged claim and evidence from original full167-group review, verified byte/hash preservation
rows.figure_or_rule: - **Capped expenses.** Qualifying-purpose spending up to 3% of total income, and only if paid to bodies carrying on those activities and used only for those purposes (art. 24). Representation up to 1%, if business-related, documented and not paid to a related person (art. 25). Memberships up to 0.1%, except a membership fixed by law (art. 26). Do not use the corporate 3.5% cap.

rows.review_basis: Unchanged claim and evidence from original full167-group review, verified byte/hash preservation
rows.figure_or_rule: - **Bad debts.** Deductible only if the debt was earlier included in income, is written off in the books and failed collection is proved; a later recovery goes back into income (art. 27). Reserve funds are not deductible (art. 28).

rows.review_basis: Unchanged claim and evidence from original full167-group review, verified byte/hash preservation
rows.figure_or_rule: - **Related-party interest.** Deductible up to the open-market interest cost and no more than actually paid (art. 30). The difference between arm's length interest and interest actually received is added to the lender's base (art. 31).

rows.review_basis: Unchanged claim and evidence from original full167-group review, verified byte/hash preservation
rows.figure_or_rule: - **Losses.** Business losses carry forward for no more than five years (art. 33). Keep a register by year of origin and use. A business loss is not set against rent, capital income or capital gains, and a capital loss is not carried forward under art. 33.

rows.review_basis: Unchanged claim and evidence from original full167-group review, verified byte/hash preservation
rows.figure_or_rule: - **Mixed-use costs.** Home office, car, phone and internet costs are deductible only for the business part, since private costs are excluded (art. 21(1)) and costs must be documented (arts. 13(2) and 21(2)). The law sets no fixed home-office or car percentage: ask for floor-area or mileage evidence and deduct nothing until it is produced.

rows.figure_or_rule: - **VAT-registered taxpayers.** Output VAT is not income and recoverable input VAT is not an expense, because the base follows the income statement (arts. 18 and 20).

rows.figure_or_rule: Rent from movable and immovable property (art. 34). Expenses are documented actual costs or, if not documented, 30% of rent (art. 35(1) and (2)). For rooms, apartments, houses and flats let to tourists, standard expenses are 50% if tourist tax was paid, or 70% under a lease with a travel agency or local tourist organisation giving average occupancy of at least 60 days a year (art. 35(3)). The route depends on the evidence, not on the larger percentage. Taxable income is rent less expenses in the same period (art. 36). A legal-person or entrepreneur tenant withholds 15% at each payment; rent received directly is taxed with the annual return (art. 49a). A licensed holiday-letting provider files a return even with no income in the year (art. 43(5)). Tourist tax, property tax and VAT are separate.

No costs are deductible; the base is the gross amount (art. 37(3) and (4)). Interest on debt securities issued by the state, the Central Bank of Montenegro or a municipality is not capital income (art. 37(5)). The payer withholds 15% at payment (art. 50).

rows.figure_or_rule: - **What.** Gains on the sale or transfer of real estate (land, buildings, flats, business units and other structures), stakes in legal persons and shares and other equity securities. A negative difference is a capital loss (art. 37a).

rows.review_basis: Unchanged claim and evidence from original full167-group review, verified byte/hash preservation
rows.figure_or_rule: - **Real estate.** Sale price is the contract price less documented reconstruction and sale costs; the tax authority sets the price if the contract price is below market, and an exchange uses market price (art. 37c). Acquisition cost is the price paid or the price the authority set on acquisition under the real-estate transfer tax law, or construction cost for a self-built property; for a gift or inheritance, the donor's or deceased's cost. It is indexed each year by retail price growth from acquisition to sale, using official statistics. Only if no cost can be established is acquisition cost 80% of the sale price (art. 37d).

rows.review_basis: Unchanged claim and evidence from original full167-group review, verified byte/hash preservation
rows.figure_or_rule: - **Company stakes.** Sale and purchase values are those in the contract; the authority sets the sale value if below market; a stake acquired on founding costs the founding contribution plus increases (art. 37e).

rows.review_basis: Unchanged claim and evidence from original full167-group review, verified byte/hash preservation
rows.figure_or_rule: - **Shares.** Listed shares cost the documented price paid; unlisted shares the documented price, or nominal value if no price is documented. Repeated purchases of the same issuer use FIFO. Bonus shares paid as a dividend cost the value at which they were acquired (art. 37f).

rows.figure_or_rule: - **Losses.** A capital loss is set only against capital gains of the same tax period (art. 37h).

rows.review_basis: Unchanged claim and evidence from original full167-group review, verified byte/hash preservation
rows.figure_or_rule: - **Tax.** 15%, computed annually and paid with the annual return (art. 50a). A gain recorded in business books goes in the tax balance, not a separate return (art. 43(6a)); never report it twice.

rows.figure_or_rule: Taxable winnings from lottery games and betting are each winning less its corresponding stake (art. 37s(2)(1) and (2)); a global jackpot uses the total accumulated prize defined in art. 37s(2)(3), without importing that stake deduction. Rates: progressive bands for winnings paid to 20 May 2026; 12% for winnings paid from 21 May 2026 ([70/26][may]). The game organiser withholds at each payment or transfer (art. 50f).

Not available to someone who closed the same or a similar activity in the previous three years, to recipients of aid for firms in difficulty, or in transport, shipbuilding, steel, trade and hospitality (except primary hospitality establishments). Apply within 30 days of registration; the authority decides; a statement of other state aid goes with each annual return.

rows.figure_or_rule: - **New hires there** (art. 32b): a permanent or at least five-year hire of a person registered with the Employment Agency for over three months and living in an underdeveloped municipality frees the salary tax for four years, if headcount rises above the 12-month average. If the employer ends the contract within five years (other than at the employee's request or for serious breach), the tax is repaid within 30 days. A person previously employed by the founder or a related person of the new employer is excluded, whether or not there was a break in employment (art. 32b(3)).

rows.figure_or_rule: - **Municipal surtax (prirez).** A municipality can levy a surtax on the PIT on salary, independent activity, property and property rights, and capital income, at up to 13% of the tax, or up to 15% in the Capital City and the Old Royal Capital (Local Self-Government Financing Law art. 8). The actual rate is the municipality's own decision (art. 9). It is a tax on the tax, never added to the income rate: at a 13% surtax the top business rate becomes 15% × 1.13 = 16.95%; at 15% it is 17.25%. The law lists only these four bases; capital gains and gambling winnings are not among them.

rows.figure_or_rule: - **Social contributions.** Employees pay 10% PIO and 0.5% unemployment; the employer pays 0% PIO and 0.5% unemployment (Contributions Law arts. 15 and 18). The health contribution provisions are deleted (art. 17). The annual PIO ceiling is set each year by Ministry of Finance act (art. 14(3) and (4)). Older secondary guides still show 15% employee pension and 8.5% health; those rates are out of date. Details, bases and the self-employed rules are in the [social contributions skill](montenegro-social-contributions.md).

A VAT-registered taxpayer cannot pay lump-sum PIT (PIT Law art. 49(12)). See the [VAT skill](montenegro-vat.md).

An overpayment is refunded on request or credited to the next year's advances (art. 42(6)).

rows.figure_or_rule: - **Lump-sum tax** (art. 49): available on request to a principal independent activity with turnover below EUR 30,000.01. Apply by the end of January, or within five days of registration for a new activity; the authority decides within 15 days. Tax is paid monthly at 1/12 by the end of the month for the previous month; seasonal activities of up to six months pay by the 5th of the month for the current month. Turnover books must be kept. Not available for lawyers, notaries, auditors, accountants, health, consulting, design, surveying, enforcement officers and other professional and intellectual activities, hairdressing, billiards and amusement games, wholesale and retail trade, hospitality, hotels, financial intermediation, real estate, or VAT-registered taxpayers; the authority can approve lump-sum tax for trade or hospitality in a kiosk, trailer or mobile unit only where the taxpayer produces and sells only its own products (art. 49(10) and (11)). If circumstances justify it, the authority orders a change of method by decision (art. 49(7)). The scale is set by Ministry rulebook (art. 49(2)).

Foreign salary uses the monthly salary bands on each month's receipts, not the annual business scale. The bases in main 3.1 to 3.6 sum to 3.7; the printed 15% row 3.8 produces 3.9.
